sections.title: Architecture
sections.content: Acceptance uses immutable, owner-local evidence artifacts. It freezes baseline/candidate identities, computes complete Consumer Closure, executes real required checks, and alone may publish acceptance-passed. Bootstrap supplies non-authorizing semantic evidence only.

sections.title: Routing
sections.content: After current required checks pass, deterministic_only is the default and launches no Bootstrap work. Focused or full Bootstrap requires an explicit Acceptance-owned --request-bootstrap record and controlled receipt; policy, risk, supervision, and advisory text cannot upgrade the route.

sections.title: Execution Safety
sections.content: Bootstrap segments have stable canonical descriptors, immutable segment-only snapshots, inherited access proofs, and no live repository traversal. Runtime recovery distinguishes liveness from effective progress, uses append-only events and conjunctive leases, and keeps transport failures non-semantic.

sections.title: Implementation Plan
sections.content: Seven ordered slices cover shared canonical evidence, consumer migration, Bootstrap runtime, Acceptance closure/checks/routes, authority projection, semantic import/finalization, and rollout regression. Required commands define RED/GREEN checks and terminal-full validates all owner-owned GREEN programs.

sections.title: Repair Scope
sections.content: Round 9 repairs three P1 findings: remove inferred Bootstrap routing, make deterministic check results machine-verifiable, and require Acceptance-owned explicit request admission. Affected slices are S3, S5, and S6, with acceptance, import, and regression validation.
